question: What further distinctions are made among practitioners who remain in the world and those who seek liberation?
premises: One practitioner follows worldly duty, desires fruit, abides in good, and avoids evil.
The seeker of liberation is also divided into types.
One type of liberation-seeker is seedless and free from pledges and related observances.
inference: Therefore practitioners are further distinguished by worldly orientation and by the seedless form of the liberation-seeker.
uncertainties: The contrast implied by dvidha for the mumukṣu is only partly stated in this verse.
plain_english: One type follows worldly duty, desires fruit, abides in what is good, and avoids what is evil. The seeker of liberation is twofold: the seedless one is free from pledges and the like.
